CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  ORDER % 16.02.2023 CRL.M.A. 4260/2023 & CRL.M.A. 4261/2023 1.
Exemption allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2. The applications stand disposed of.
CRL.M.C. 1116/2023 AND CRL.M.A. 4259/2023 3.

Petitioner has filed this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No. 372/2016,
under Section 498A IPC, registered at Police StationSec-23 Dwarka, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.
4.
Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State enters appearance and accepts notice.

5. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner and respondent no.2 got married on 18.02.2000 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as wife and husband with each other.
After the marriage, disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately.
A daughter and a son were born out of the said wedlock.
On 05.02.2016, respondent no.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that during the pendency of the trial, parties have settled the matter amicably out of court and decided to live happily and harmoniously together.
The said settlement was reduced in writing on 12.02.2023 by putting an end to all the disputes and differences.
A copy of the said Compromise Deed is on record.
7. Petitioner and respondent no.2 are present in Court today and they have been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.

Respondent no.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioner and she is living happily with her husband at 102, Sadoday Mansarovar Appartment, Vijay Nagar Road, Raj Nagar, Nagpur, Maharashtra - 440013 with their children.
She further submits that the settlement/compromise has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
Respondent no.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
8. Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.

9. Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, and parties are living together along with their children, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.
Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No. 372/2016, under Section 498A IPC, registered at Police StationSec-23 Dwarka, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
10. The present petition along with pending application stands disposed of accordingly.

RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J FEBRUARY 16, 2023 p Kishore Chaudhary vs The State Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114725383/
